result.builder:
Add a --tsv flag to the csv2json CLI so it reads tab-separated input. Make one pull request that meets every acceptance line below.

Current state: bin/csv2json.js reads stdin and calls parse(text) with no separator, and it ignores argv. src/parse.js exports parse(text, sep = ','). test/csv.test.js uses node:test and already has a 'cli' test that runs bin/csv2json.js with execFileSync. package.json has "test": "node --test". README.md documents only CSV usage.

Steps:
1. In bin/csv2json.js, check whether '--tsv' appears anywhere in process.argv.slice(2). If it does, call parse(text, '	'). If it does not, call parse(text) exactly as today. Leave the output format as it is: JSON.stringify of the array, then a single '
'.
2. Do not change how fields are split (no quoting rules), do not add auto-detection, --sep/--delimiter or --help, and do not change how unknown arguments are handled. Leave src/parse.js alone unless you really have to change it, and if you do, the CSV behaviour must stay the same.
3. In test/csv.test.js (or a new test/*.test.js file), add node:test tests that run bin/csv2json.js with the argument '--tsv' through execFileSync on input with tabs and assert the exact stdout. Cover: 'a	b
1	2
' -> '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
'; 'name	note
x	hello, world
' -> '[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]
'; and 'a	b
1	2
3	4
' -> '[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]
'. Also add a test that tab input without the flag still gives '[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]
' (a JSON tab escape inside the key and value). Keep the existing tests.
4. In README.md, add a section for the --tsv flag. Say that it reads tab-separated input and give the example invocation `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`. Keep the existing CSV example.
5. From the repo root, run `npm test` and check that it exits 0. Run each acceptance command below by hand and check that the output is byte-exact.

Acceptance lines (all must hold):
- `printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline and exits 0.
- With --tsv, commas inside a field stay literal: `printf 'name	note
x	hello, world
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]` followed by a newline.
- With --tsv and several data rows, every row comes out in order: `printf 'a	b
1	2
3	4
' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]` followed by a newline.
- Without the flag, CSV still works as before: `printf 'a,b
1,2
' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline.
- Without the flag, tabs are not treated as separators: `printf 'a	b
1	2
' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a	b":"1	2"}]` followed by a newline, which is the current output.
- `npm test` exits 0, and test/ contains at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-separated input and checks its output.
- README.md documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request head against each acceptance line, in order. Run every command from the repository root in bash; the commands use process substitution. `cmp` prints nothing and the command prints SAME only when the bytes match exactly, including the single trailing newline.

Check 1. Line: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline and exits 0.
Run:
printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv > /tmp/o1; echo "exit=$?"; printf '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n' | cmp - /tmp/o1 && echo SAME
PASS: the output shows exit=0 and SAME. FAIL: any other exit code, or cmp reports a difference.

Check 2. Line: With --tsv, commas inside a field stay literal: `printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]` followed by a newline.
Run:
printf 'name\tnote\nx\thello, world\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv | cmp - <(printf '[{"name":"x","note":"hello, world"}]\n') && echo SAME
PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: cmp reports a difference.

Check 3. Line: With --tsv and several data rows, every row comes out in order: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]` followed by a newline.
Run:
printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n3\t4\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv | cmp - <(printf '[{"a":"1","b":"2"},{"a":"3","b":"4"}]\n') && echo SAME
PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: cmp reports a difference.

Check 4. Line: Without the flag, CSV still works as before: `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]` followed by a newline.
Run:
printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | cmp - <(printf '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]\n') && echo SAME
PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: cmp reports a difference.

Check 5. Line: Without the flag, tabs are not treated as separators: `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` prints exactly `[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]` followed by a newline, which is the current output.
Run:
printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js | cmp - <(printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n') && echo SAME
Here the expected text has a literal backslash-t, which is the JSON tab escape. PASS: SAME is printed. FAIL: cmp reports a difference.

Check 6. Line: `npm test` exits 0, and test/ contains at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab-separated input and checks its output.
Run:
npm test; echo "exit=$?"
Then run:
grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js
Read each matching test.
PASS: exit=0, and at least one test in test/ runs bin/csv2json.js with the '--tsv' argument on input that contains tab characters and asserts on its stdout. FAIL: a non-zero exit, no match, or no matching test that both runs the CLI with --tsv on tab input and checks its output.

Check 7. Line: README.md documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation.
Run:
grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md
Then read README.md.
PASS: README.md describes the --tsv flag and contains an example invocation that uses it, such as `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`. FAIL: the flag is not mentioned, or no example invocation uses it.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- Look at whether the flag works when other arguments are also present, for example `node bin/csv2json.js x --tsv`.
- Look at whether the README says that --tsv means tab-separated input.
- The diff should not add quoting rules, --sep, auto-detection or --help, and should not change the JSON output format.
